form.title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
form.question: Did the aggregate value of your foreign financial accounts exceed $10,000 at any time during the tax year?
form.notes: NOT AN IRS FORM AND NOT PART OF THE RETURN. Filed electronically with Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. The Instructions for Schedule B say: 'If you checked the “Yes” box to Question 2 on line 7a, you must electronically file FinCEN Form 114 with Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. A U.S. person that has a financial interest in or signature authority over foreign financial accounts must file the form if the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeds $10,000 at any time during 2025. Do not attach FinCEN Form 114 to your tax return.' Penalty, verbatim: 'you may have to pay a civil penalty up to $10,000. A person who willfully fails to report an account or provide account identifying information may be subject to a civil penalty equal to the greater of $100,000 or 50% of the balance in the account at the time of the violation.' It produces no 1040 line; Schedule B line 7a is the only place the return asks about it. No revision was read - this part did not fetch the FinCEN form.
